issues.t: CVT damage when the fluid gets low
issues.sym: Whining or grinding from the transmission, slipping, shuddering, a check engine light, or a transmission fluid spot under the car.
issues.why: On front-drive models with the CVT, a fluid leak or low fluid level can let the internal pulleys and drive chain get damaged. GM issued bulletins for CVT fluid leaks and for checking pulley and chain damage.
issues.next: If you see transmission fluid under the car or hear new whining, have it checked right away. Catching a leak early can save the transmission.

issues.t: Sudden loss of drive or reduced propulsion
issues.sym: The vehicle suddenly loses power to the wheels or will barely move, often with a warning message, while the engine keeps running.
issues.why: GM bulletins trace many of these cases to the transmission valve body, which dealers are told to replace first before checking the rest of the transmission.
issues.next: Get safely out of traffic. Have it towed to a dealer and ask about GM bulletins 21-NA-003 and 24-NA-009.

issues.t: Shift to Park message and no start
issues.sym: A 'Shift to Park' message stays on after you have put it in Park and turned it off, the car won't shut down fully, or it won't restart.
issues.why: The Park switch inside the shifter can fail. GM put out a bulletin for this message with code B000A and covers shifter replacement.
issues.next: Try moving the shifter out of Park and back firmly. If it keeps happening, have the dealer check the shifter under bulletin 23-NA-119.

issues.t: Oil leak from a porous cylinder head
issues.sym: Oil seeping from the top of the engine, oil spots under the car, or a burning oil smell.
issues.why: Some cylinder heads have tiny pores in the casting that let oil seep through. GM issued a repair so the engine does not have to be replaced.
issues.next: Have the leak traced. If it is the head, ask the dealer about bulletin 23-NA-122.

issues.t: Turbo wastegate rattle and low boost
issues.sym: A rattle from the engine, often on a cold start, with lower power and a check engine light (code P0299).
issues.why: The turbo's wastegate regulator valve can wear or stick. GM tells dealers to test that valve before replacing the turbo.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the wastegate tested. Fixing the valve can avoid a full turbo replacement.

issues.t: Power loss in extreme cold
issues.sym: In very cold weather the engine runs poorly or loses power, with a check engine light and boost codes.
issues.why: Moisture can freeze into ice or sludge in the charge air cooler or crankcase ventilation. GM issued bulletins for this.
issues.next: Have the dealer check for bulletin 21-NA-293 and any updates.

issues.t: EVAP purge pump failure
issues.sym: Check engine light with evaporative system codes.
issues.why: The evaporative emissions purge pump can fail. GM put out a special coverage and a bulletin for replacement.
issues.next: Ask a Buick dealer whether your VIN is under the purge pump special coverage before paying for it.

issues.t: Roof leak causing electrical problems
issues.sym: Water on the headliner or floor, odd electrical faults, radio glitches, stalling or a no-start.
issues.why: Some vehicles were built with sealant missing on the roof, letting water in onto wiring and modules.
issues.next: Dry the interior and have the dealer check the roof seams under bulletin 20-NA-121 before modules are damaged.

issues.t: Oil pressure warning code won't clear
issues.sym: A check engine light with oil pressure code P0521 that stays on even after the problem is fixed.
issues.why: Engine computer software could keep the code stored. GM issued an emissions recall and a wiring bulletin for this code.
issues.next: Check your oil level first. Then ask a dealer about the free software update for P0521.

issues.t: Lane keep and safety alerts act up
issues.sym: Lane keep or forward collision indicators flash or show unavailable, or lane assist steers or warns when it should not.
issues.why: GM noted indicators flashing when the systems are off, and owners report lane assist faults. A dirty windshield or camera that needs calibration can also cause it.
issues.next: Keep the windshield clean in front of the camera. If faults continue, have the dealer check for software updates and calibrate the camera.

issues.t: Front brake squeal
issues.sym: A squeal from the front brakes during light braking.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for front brake squeal on light pedal use.
issues.next: Ask the dealer about bulletin 22-NA-095; the fix usually involves new pads.

issues.t: Service power steering message
issues.sym: A 'Service Power Steering' message with steering code C0051.
issues.why: GM traced this to the steering wheel angle sensor.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. Have the dealer read the code and follow bulletin 21-NA-177.

issues.t: Loose cylinder head bolts
issues.sym: Usually none at first; a loose head can lead to oil or coolant leaks.
issues.why: GM found that the outer cylinder head bolts on some 1.3L engines were not tightened at the factory and opened a dealer campaign.
issues.next: Check your VIN with a Buick dealer and have the bolts checked free.

issues.t: Engine sputters, stalls or runs rough
issues.sym: The engine sputters when you accelerate, idles rough, stalls, or won't start, sometimes with erratic shifting or a jumping fuel gauge.
issues.why: Owners report sputtering, and GM bulletins cover no-start, stalling and rough idle complaints with various codes.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Have the codes read right away and note when it happens. Ask the dealer to check for the latest bulletins and software.

issues.t: Cruise control won't set after braking
issues.sym: Cruise control will not set or resume after you have touched the brakes.
issues.why: GM found the brake pedal or its switch can cause this and tells dealers to test and replace the pedal.
issues.next: Ask the dealer about bulletin 22-NA-097.

issues.t: AWD service message
issues.sym: A service AWD message, with all-wheel drive not working.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for service messages linked to rear drive motor code C0095.
issues.next: Have the codes read at a dealer and ask about bulletin 23-NA-104.

issues.t: Auto stop/start stops working
issues.sym: The engine no longer shuts off at stops, with a check engine light and code P2797.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for stop/start not working with this code, which points to the transmission's auxiliary fluid pump circuit.
issues.next: This is not urgent. Have the dealer check bulletin 19-NA-200 at your next visit.

issues.t: Loss of brake assist (recall)
issues.sym: A brake warning message and a much firmer brake pedal.
issues.why: Contamination at a sensor connection in the electronic brake booster can cut communication and remove power assist.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Press the brake harder if this happens and get it checked. Check your VIN for recall 20V-588; the dealer replaces the brake boost module free.

issues.t: Front seat bolts may be missing (recall)
issues.sym: A front seat rocks or moves at the back.
issues.why: The rear attachment bolts for a front seat may not have been installed.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 20V-537. The dealer installs the bolts free.

issues.t: Emergency jack can break (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom while driving; the jack can crack when used to lift the vehicle.
issues.why: The spare tire jack can fracture if it is not placed exactly as the owner's manual shows.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 21V-440. The dealer replaces the jack free.

issues.t: Instrument display can go blank (recall)
issues.sym: The driver's display goes black, then comes back, at startup or while driving.
issues.why: Software in the digital instrument cluster module can make the display drop out.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: you may not see your speed or warning lights, so ease off, keep a safe distance, and pull over where it's safe. Restarting the car once parked may bring the display back; if it doesn't, have it fixed before you drive again. Check your VIN for recall 23V-744. The dealer or an over-the-air update fixes it free.

issues.t: Backup camera image blank or distorted (recall)
issues.sym: The rear camera picture flickers, looks distorted, or stays black when reversing.
issues.why: The rearview camera can fail to show a proper image.
issues.next: Look over your shoulder when backing up and check your VIN for recall 26V-539. The dealer replaces the camera free if needed.
